text:
maya: kicking off canary split to 10% on eu-gpu for the new k8s service mesh config. infra-bot just started the rollout :rocket:
infra-bot: [deploy] canary rollout started for service=gpu-runtime namespace=inference weight=10% via splitter v2. command: `kubectl apply -f canary-splitter.yaml`
jorge: seeing 502s from canary pods already? what do the pod logs show? :thinking:
sre-oncall: looked at envoy logs -> upstream error: no healthy endpoints for cluster "svc-gpu-runtime-eu". DNS for svc-gpu-runtime-eu shows short TTLs and intermittent NXDOMAIN.
maya: NXDOMAIN? that's odd. we didn't change kube-dns in this rollout. any recent node reshard/scale events?
leo: cloud infra had a reshard operation earlier to rebalance endpoints across AZs (auto rebalancer ran at ~08:10 UTC). looks like kube-proxy endpoints were momentarily inconsistent during the reshard. also saw spikes in cloud-provider API errors: 429s for endpoint updates.
tara: 429s -> rate limit from provider, probably due to simultaneous endpoint updates from the rebalancer + argocd syncs. argocd had 3 concurrent syncs to the same svc due to parallel apps.
sam: can we temporarily freeze the canary weight and pause further splits until endpoints converge? reduce to 0% if unhealthy?
maya: doing that now: patching splitter to rollback weight to 0%. `kubectl patch traffic-split gpu-runtime -p '{"spec":{"backends":[{"weight":"100"}]}}'`
infra-bot: [action] traffic-split patched -> canary weight 0%, primary 100%.
jorge: good. next steps: 1) throttle argocd syncs for the service to avoid concurrent endpoint churn, 2) add a short jitter to the rebalancer, 3) add retry/backoff on endpoint writes in our control-plane syncer.
leo: adding terraform change request to set provider endpoint throttle to 5r/s for endpoint updates and adding a small sleep in the reshard job. will open PR shortly.
tara: for short term can we increase readinessProbe timeout and reduce failure threshold so pods stay 'ready' during brief DNS blips? risk is masking real failures though.
sam: i'd prefer not to mask; let's set readinessProbe to be slightly more forgiving (periodSeconds 10 -> 15) for this rollout only. add to canary override values in helm: `readinessProbe: { periodSeconds: 15, failureThreshold: 5 }`
maya: agreed. also adding a temporary argocd app freeze label: `argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "1000"` to ensure it syncs last.
jorge: created ticket INF-4123 to add endpoint-write backoff and a circuit-breaker for reshard jobs. linking PRs in the ticket.
leo: PR 584 opened for terraform provider throttle change, assigning to @tara for review.
tara: reviewing now. will also add a small doc note about not running multiple app syncs against core svc in parallel.
sre-oncall: monitoring - error rates returned to baseline within ~4m after splitter patch and readiness tweak. no user-facing impact reported. :thumbsup:
maya: thanks everyone. follow-up: schedule a postmortem to tweak GitOps sync concurrency and add canary guardrail that aborts on cluster endpoint instability. I'll post a short RFC in #eng-infra tomorrow.
infra-bot: [incident] INF-4123 created: "Endpoint reshard + argocd concurrent sync -> canary oscillation" assigned to eng-infra.
jorge: note for retro: consider adding a health-check upstream for 'endpoints stable' before split weight changes. canary safety net.
maya: good note. closing thread for now, reopening if we see reoccurrence. :white_check_mark:
